The Hellinger affinity of the actual averaged Gaussian targets is the k-th power of their actual single-block affinity. \int_{\mathbb R^d}\sqrt{ rac{d ar\pi_+}{dx} rac{d ar\pi_-}{dx}}\,dx=\left(\int_{\mathbb R^n}\sqrt{p_+(x)p_-(x)}\,dxight)^k=a^k. \(d,n\in\mathbb N,\ 3\le n\le d,\ \kappa\ge4\); set \(k=\lfloor d/nfloor\) and \(r=d-kn=d mod n\). Both endpoint inequalities are inclusive. For normalized full orthogonal Haar probability \(\mu_n\), let \(
u_\pm=2\mu_n|_{\{\det O=\pm1\}}\). Define \(A_O= rac{\kappa+1}{2}I- rac{\kappa-1}{4}(O+O^	op)\), \(\mathcal D_\pm=( oldsymbol O\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(A_{O_1},\ldots,A_{O_k},I_r))_\#
u_\pm^{\otimes k}\), and the actual averaged targets \( ar\pi_\pm=\int\mathcal N(0,A^{-1})\,d\mathcal D_\pm(A)\). Each product uses one common sign. Use the actual block density representatives \(p_\pm(x)=\int \sqrt{\det A_O}(2\pi)^{-n/2}e^{-x^	op A_Ox/2}\,d
u_\pm(O)\), and \(a=\int_{\mathbb R^n}\sqrt{p_+(x)p_-(x)}\,dx\). Actual Gaussian validity, Haar-average inner L1, nonnegativity, measurability and normalization are supplied internally by canonical producers. All base measures are canonical Euclidean Lebesgue volume. Put \(R_\pm=d ar\pi_\pm/dx\). The exact Lean integrand is \(F(x)=\sqrt{\operatorname{toReal}(R_+(x))\operatorname{toReal}(R_-(x))}\). RN derivatives are a.e. representatives. Actual Ex70 densities prove their finite a.e. identification, so neither the RN nonexistence default nor the totalized \(\operatorname{toReal}(\infty)=0\) changes the asserted integral. The literal contiguous split sends ambient volume to the product block/residual volumes. For \(r>0\), the common residual factor is \(\varphi_r(z)=(2\pi)^{-r/2}e^{-\lVert zVert^2/2}\). For \(r=0\), its sole vector has unit volume and \(\varphi_0=1\), realizing the source omitted-factor convention. No positive-remainder premise, supplied density identity or supplied affinity-integrability premise is added.

    {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 4 ≤ κ),
    letI : MeasurableSpace (Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) := borel _
    let e : ((Fin n × Fin (d / n)) ⊕ Fin (d % n)) ≃ Fin d :=
      ((Equiv.sumCongr
        ((Equiv.prodComm (Fin n) (Fin (d / n))).trans finProdFinEquiv)
        (Equiv.refl (Fin (d % n)))).trans finSumFinEquiv).trans
        (finCongr (by simpa [Nat.mul_comm] using Nat.div_add_mod d n))
    let B : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ :=
      fun O => ((κ + 1) / 2) • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) -
        ((κ - 1) / 4) • ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) +
          (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose)
    let μ := (Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ)))
    let νpos := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
      {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = 1}
    let νneg := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
      {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = -1}
    let Dpos := (Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (d / n) => νpos)).map (fun Os : Fin (d / n) → Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ => Matrix.reindex e e
      (Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun j => B (Os j))) 0 0
        (1 : Matrix (Fin (d % n)) (Fin (d % n)) ℝ)))
    let Dneg := (Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (d / n) => νneg)).map (fun Os : Fin (d / n) → Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ => Matrix.reindex e e
      (Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun j => B (Os j))) 0 0
        (1 : Matrix (Fin (d % n)) (Fin (d % n)) ℝ)))
    let γ : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ → Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :=
      fun A => multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) A⁻¹
    let Mpos := Dpos.bind γ
    let Mneg := Dneg.bind γ
    let p : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ :=
      fun O x => Real.sqrt (B O).det /
        (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) *
        Real.exp (-((WithLp.ofLp x) ⬝ᵥ
          (B O *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x)) / 2)
    let qpos : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun x => ∫ O, p O x ∂νpos
    let qneg : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun x => ∫ O, p O x ∂νneg
    let a : ℝ := ∫ x, Real.sqrt (qpos x * qneg x)
    let F : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ := fun x =>
      Real.sqrt (((Mpos.rnDeriv volume) x).toReal * ((Mneg.rnDeriv volume) x).toReal)
    Mpos ≪ volume ∧ Mneg ≪ volume ∧ Integrable F volume ∧
      (∫ x, F x) = a ^ (d / n)

blind_reconstruction.text:
For every pair of natural numbers d and n with 3 ≤ n ≤ d, and every real number κ ≥ 4, make the following constructions. Put k = d / n = floor(d/n) and r = d % n, so d = nk + r. Work with the usual real Euclidean spaces, Lebesgue measures, Borel structures, and the Borel structure on the real d by d matrix space.

Let G = O(n), the full real orthogonal group. Let μ be its Haar probability measure, normalized on all of G, and define ν₊ = 2 μ restricted to {O in G : det O = 1} and ν₋ = 2 μ restricted to {O in G : det O = -1}. The factor 2 is scalar multiplication of the restricted measure. For O in G define the real symmetric matrix
B(O) = ((κ + 1)/2) I_n - ((κ - 1)/4)(O + Oᵀ).
Define the coordinate equivalence e : ((Fin n × Fin k) ⊕ Fin r) → Fin d by e(inl(i,j)) = jn + i and e(inr(t)) = nk + t. Thus its reindexing places the kth collection of n-dimensional blocks in consecutive coordinate groups, followed by r remaining coordinates; more precisely block j occupies coordinates jn through jn+n-1 for 0 ≤ j < k.

For each sign s in {+, -}, take the actual finite independent product measure ν_s^{⊗k} on tuples (O_j)_{j in Fin k} in G^k. Send a tuple to A = reindex(e,e)(diag_blocks((B(O_j))_j, I_r)), where the entries between different n-dimensional blocks, and between those blocks and the remainder block, are zero. Let D_s be the pushforward measure on real d by d matrices. All k matrices O_j in the plus construction have determinant +1 under their sampling measure, and all k in the minus construction have determinant -1; their signs are not independently selected from both components. For each real d by d matrix A let γ(A) = multivariateGaussian(0,A⁻¹), using the total matrix inverse and the specified Gaussian constructor. Define M₊ = D₊.bind γ and M₋ = D₋.bind γ. These are the mixtures of centered Gaussians with the displayed random precision matrices. Under the present parameter assumptions B(O) is positive definite for every O in G, as are all matrices in the defining image of the block map, so their inverses have the ordinary covariance meaning. The identity remainder block is allowed also when r=0, with the approved zero-dimensional conventions.

For x in real n-dimensional Euclidean space, write v=WithLp.ofLp(x) for its coordinate vector and define
p(O,x) = sqrt(det B(O)) / (2π)^(n/2) · exp(-(vᵀ B(O) v)/2),
where n/2 in this normalization is real division. Define the real functions q₊(x) = ∫_G p(O,x) dν₊(O) and q₋(x) = ∫_G p(O,x) dν₋(O), and the real number
a = ∫_{R^n} sqrt(q₊(x) q₋(x)) dx.
These are the displayed one-block mixture-density constructions. Every unqualified Euclidean integral here is with respect to its canonical Lebesgue measure, and the real integrals use the approved totalized Bochner integral convention.

For x in real d-dimensional Euclidean space define
F(x) = sqrt(toReal((dM₊/dvolume)(x)) · toReal((dM₋/dvolume)(x))),
where each derivative is exactly the canonical ENNReal-valued Measure.rnDeriv from the statement, and toReal is applied separately before multiplication and square root. In particular toReal maps an infinite derivative value to 0. The derivative constructors are totalized as described in the input context and specify measurable representatives; density interpretations and uniqueness concern Lebesgue almost everywhere, rather than pointwise identification with any separately displayed formula.

Then M₊ is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on R^d, M₋ is absolutely continuous with respect to that same measure, F is genuinely Lebesgue integrable, and
∫_{R^d} F(x) dx = a^k = a^(d / n).
The final exponent is the natural-number quotient k, using an integer power of the real number a. No extra factor involving the remainder r appears. The explicit integrability conclusion is for F; totality of the earlier real integral constructors by itself is not an additional integrability assertion. The result does not separately assert everywhere-finite RN derivatives or pointwise equality of the canonical RN representatives with a named density. All constructions are fixed by d, n, and κ; there are no additional choices of measures, matrices, constants, or representatives to quantify over.

import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.ProductDensity
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.InformationTheory.DensityAffinity
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Pi
open Matrix MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped ENNReal BigOperators
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.OrthogonalHaar
open AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.DeterminantFamily
/-!
# Actual Gaussian-mixture Hellinger-affinity tensorization

Zhou--Suzuki, arXiv:2610.20492v1, Appendix B.2.3 Ex71. The two laws
are the actual matrix-prior Gaussian binds. Their canonical ambient-volume
Radon--Nikodym derivatives agree a.e. with the actual Ex70 product densities;
the real conversion therefore represents finite densities, independently of
null-set choices. Normalized product densities give genuine L1 affinity.
The volume-preserving contiguous split, finite-product Fubini and common
residual normalization yield the exact power of the actual block affinity.
The argument includes the zero-dimensional omitted-residual convention.
Amplified TV Ex72 and the oracle/query lower bounds remain separate.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.AffinityTensorization
set_option autoImplicit false
theorem actual_affinity_tensorization {d n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hnd : n ≤ d)
    {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 4 ≤ κ) :
    letI : MeasurableSpace (Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) := borel _
    let μ := orthogonalHaar n
    let νpos := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
      {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = 1}
    let νneg := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
      {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = -1}
    let Dpos := (Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (d / n) => νpos)).map (blockPrecision κ)
    let Dneg := (Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (d / n) => νneg)).map (blockPrecision κ)
    let γ : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ → Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :=
      fun A => multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) A⁻¹
    let Mpos := Dpos.bind γ
    let Mneg := Dneg.bind γ
    let p : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ :=
      fun O x => Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det /
        (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) *
        Real.exp (-((WithLp.ofLp x) ⬝ᵥ
          (singleBlockPrecision κ O *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x)) / 2)
    let qpos : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun x => ∫ O, p O x ∂νpos
    let qneg : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun x => ∫ O, p O x ∂νneg
    let a : ℝ := ∫ x, Real.sqrt (qpos x * qneg x)
    let F : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ := fun x =>
      Real.sqrt (((Mpos.rnDeriv volume) x).toReal * ((Mneg.rnDeriv volume) x).toReal)
    Mpos ≪ volume ∧ Mneg ≪ volume ∧ Integrable F volume ∧
      (∫ x, F x) = a ^ (d / n) := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let : MeasurableSpace (Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) := borel _
  let μ := orthogonalHaar n
  let νpos := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
    {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = 1}
  let νneg := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
    {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = -1}
  let Dpos := (Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (d / n) => νpos)).map (blockPrecision κ)
  let Dneg := (Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (d / n) => νneg)).map (blockPrecision κ)
  let γ : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ → Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :=
    fun A => multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) A⁻¹
  let Mpos := Dpos.bind γ
  let Mneg := Dneg.bind γ
  let p : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ :=
    fun O x => Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det /
      (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) *
      Real.exp (-((WithLp.ofLp x) ⬝ᵥ
        (singleBlockPrecision κ O *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x)) / 2)
  let qpos : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun x => ∫ O, p O x ∂νpos
  let qneg : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun x => ∫ O, p O x ∂νneg
  let a : ℝ := ∫ x, Real.sqrt (qpos x * qneg x)
  let F : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ := fun x =>
    Real.sqrt (((Mpos.rnDeriv volume) x).toReal * ((Mneg.rnDeriv volume) x).toReal)
  let e : ((Fin n × Fin (d / n)) ⊕ Fin (d % n)) ≃ Fin d :=
    ((Equiv.sumCongr
      ((Equiv.prodComm (Fin n) (Fin (d / n))).trans finProdFinEquiv)
      (Equiv.refl (Fin (d % n)))).trans finSumFinEquiv).trans
      (finCongr (by simpa [Nat.mul_comm] using Nat.div_add_mod d n))
  let X := (Fin (d / n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) ×
    EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (d % n))
  let split : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → X :=
    fun x => (fun j => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => x (e (Sum.inl (i, j)))),
      WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => x (e (Sum.inr i))))
  let φ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (d % n)) → ℝ :=
    fun z => (2 * Real.pi) ^ (-((d % n : ℕ) : ℝ) / 2) * Real.exp (-‖z‖ ^ 2 / 2)
  let Qpos : X → ℝ := fun y => (∏ j, qpos (y.1 j)) * φ y.2
  let Qneg : X → ℝ := fun y => (∏ j, qneg (y.1 j)) * φ y.2
  let G : X → ℝ := fun y => Real.sqrt (Qpos y * Qneg y)
  let r : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun x => Real.sqrt (qpos x * qneg x)
  -- Both actual laws and the coordinate-volume identity use the same Ex70 node.
  have hp := ProductDensity.actual_product_density hn hnd hκ (b := 1) (Or.inl rfl)
  have hn' := ProductDensity.actual_product_density hn hnd hκ (b := -1) (Or.inr rfl)
  have hvol : MeasurePreserving split volume volume := hp.1
  have hP0 : ∀ y, 0 ≤ Qpos y := hp.2.1
  have hN0 : ∀ y, 0 ≤ Qneg y := hn'.2.1
  have hPm : Measurable Qpos := hp.2.2.1
  have hNm : Measurable Qneg := hn'.2.2.1
  have hPi : Integrable Qpos volume := hp.2.2.2.1
  have hNi : Integrable Qneg volume := hn'.2.2.2.1
  have hP1 : (∫ y, Qpos y) = 1 := hp.2.2.2.2.1
  have hN1 : (∫ y, Qneg y) = 1 := hn'.2.2.2.2.1
  have hPD : Mpos = volume.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (Qpos (split x))) :=
    hp.2.2.2.2.2.2.1
  have hND : Mneg = volume.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (Qneg (split x))) :=
    hn'.2.2.2.2.2.2.1
  have hPmA : Measurable (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (Qpos (split x))) :=
    ENNReal.measurable_ofReal.comp (hPm.comp hvol.measurable)
  have hNmA : Measurable (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (Qneg (split x))) :=
    ENNReal.measurable_ofReal.comp (hNm.comp hvol.measurable)
  have hPRN : Mpos.rnDeriv volume =ᵐ[volume]
      (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (Qpos (split x))) := by
    rw [hPD]
    exact Measure.rnDeriv_withDensity volume hPmA
  have hNRN : Mneg.rnDeriv volume =ᵐ[volume]
      (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (Qneg (split x))) := by
    rw [hND]
    exact Measure.rnDeriv_withDensity volume hNmA
  -- In particular these actual derivatives are finite a.e.; toReal uses no fallback.
  have hFG : F =ᵐ[volume] G ∘ split := by
    filter_upwards [hPRN, hNRN] with x hpx hnx
    dsimp only [F, Function.comp_def, G]
    rw [hpx, hnx, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (hP0 _), ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (hN0 _)]
  have hGi : Integrable G volume :=
    (AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.InformationTheory.DensityAffinity.normalized_density_tv_affinity
      volume hP0 hN0 hPm hNm hPi hNi hP1 hN1).1
  have hGm : Measurable G := (hPm.mul hNm).sqrt
  have htrans : (∫ x, G (split x)) = ∫ y, G y := by
    have h := integral_map_of_stronglyMeasurable (μ := volume)
      hvol.measurable hGm.stronglyMeasurable
    rw [hvol.map_eq] at h
    exact h.symm
  have hm := MixtureDensities.actual_mixture_densities hn hκ
  rcases hm with ⟨hq0, _, _, _, _, hqp1, _, _, _⟩
  have hqpos0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ qpos x := fun x => (hq0 x).1
  have hqneg0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ qneg x := fun x => (hq0 x).2
  have hqpos1 : (∫ x, qpos x) = 1 := hqp1
  have hφ0 (z : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (d % n))) : 0 ≤ φ z := by
    dsimp [φ]
    positivity
  -- Unit mass of the common residual follows from the actual normalized Ex70
  -- density and unit mass of each block, including the zero-dimensional case.
  have hblocks1 : (∫ y : Fin (d / n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n),
      ∏ j, qpos (y j)) = 1 := by
    rw [integral_fintype_prod_volume_eq_pow, hqpos1, one_pow]
  have hφ1 : (∫ z, φ z) = 1 := by
    have h : (∫ y : X, Qpos y) =
        (∫ y : Fin (d / n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), ∏ j, qpos (y j)) *
          (∫ z, φ z) := by
      simpa only [Qpos, X, Measure.volume_eq_prod] using
        (integral_prod_mul (μ := volume) (ν := volume)
          (fun y : Fin (d / n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) => ∏ j, qpos (y j)) φ)
    rw [hP1, hblocks1, one_mul] at h
    exact h.symm
  have hfactor (y : X) : G y = (∏ j, r (y.1 j)) * φ y.2 := by
    have heq : Qpos y * Qneg y =
        (∏ j, qpos (y.1 j) * qneg (y.1 j)) * (φ y.2) ^ 2 := by
      dsimp [Qpos, Qneg]
      rw [Finset.prod_mul_distrib]
      ring
    dsimp only [G]
    rw [heq, Real.sqrt_mul (Finset.prod_nonneg (fun j _ =>
      mul_nonneg (hqpos0 _) (hqneg0 _))), Real.sqrt_sq (hφ0 _),
      Real.sqrt_prod _ (fun j _ => mul_nonneg (hqpos0 _) (hqneg0 _))]
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · change Mpos ≪ volume
    rw [hPD]
    exact withDensity_absolutelyContinuous _ _
  · change Mneg ≪ volume
    rw [hND]
    exact withDensity_absolutelyContinuous _ _
  · exact (hvol.integrable_comp_of_integrable hGi).congr hFG.symm
  · calc
      (∫ x, F x) = ∫ x, G (split x) := integral_congr_ae hFG
      _ = ∫ y, G y := htrans
      _ = ∫ y : X, (∏ j, r (y.1 j)) * φ y.2 :=
        integral_congr_ae (Filter.Eventually.of_forall hfactor)
      _ = (∫ y : Fin (d / n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), ∏ j, r (y j)) *
          (∫ z, φ z) := by
        simpa only [X, Measure.volume_eq_prod] using
          (integral_prod_mul (μ := volume) (ν := volume)
            (fun y : Fin (d / n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) => ∏ j, r (y j)) φ)
      _ = a ^ (d / n) := by
        rw [hφ1, mul_one, integral_fintype_prod_volume_eq_pow]
        simp only [Fintype.card_fin]
        rfl

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.AffinityTensorization

Define \(A_O=\frac{\kappa+1}{2}I-\frac{\kappa-1}{4}(O+O^\top)\), \(\mathcal D_\pm=(\boldsymbol O\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(A_{O_1},\ldots,A_{O_k},I_r))_\#\nu_\pm^{\otimes k}\), and the actual averaged targets \(\bar\pi_\pm=\int\mathcal N(0,A^{-1})\,d\mathcal D_\pm(A)\). Each product uses one common sign.

Use the actual block density representatives \(p_\pm(x)=\int \sqrt{\det A_O}(2\pi)^{-n/2}e^{-x^\top A_Ox/2}\,d\nu_\pm(O)\), and \(a=\int_{\mathbb R^n}\sqrt{p_+(x)p_-(x)}\,dx\). Actual Gaussian validity, Haar-average inner L1, nonnegativity, measurability and normalization are supplied internally by canonical producers.

All base measures are canonical Euclidean Lebesgue volume. Put \(R_\pm=d\bar\pi_\pm/dx\). The exact Lean integrand is \(F(x)=\sqrt{\operatorname{toReal}(R_+(x))\operatorname{toReal}(R_-(x))}\). RN derivatives are a.e. representatives. Actual Ex70 densities prove their finite a.e. identification, so neither the RN nonexistence default nor the totalized \(\operatorname{toReal}(\infty)=0\) changes the asserted integral.

The literal contiguous split sends ambient volume to the product block/residual volumes. For \(r>0\), the common residual factor is \(\varphi_r(z)=(2\pi)^{-r/2}e^{-\lVert z\rVert^2/2}\). For \(r=0\), its sole vector has unit volume and \(\varphi_0=1\), realizing the source omitted-factor convention. No positive-remainder premise, supplied density identity or supplied affinity-integrability premise is added.

notation.text: The two laws are actual precision-prior Gaussian mixtures; block densities are their genuine Haar averages. Ambient RN derivatives are identified a.e. before real conversion.

steps.title: Use the actual Ex70 densities for both signs
steps.text: Apply the same canonical actual product-density theorem twice, for the positive and negative Haar components. It identifies each true matrix-prior Gaussian bind with its ambient density and supplies the common volume-preserving split. All density conditions come from these actual laws.
steps.lean: hp/hn' call ProductDensity.actual_product_density. hvol, hP0/hN0, hPm/hNm, hPi/hNi, hP1/hN1 and hPD/hND project the actual volume, L1, unit mass and ambient density certificates.

steps.title: Identify the intrinsic RN representatives
steps.text: The actual density equalities imply absolute continuity. RN uniqueness for a measurable density over sigma-finite Euclidean volume gives a.e. equality with ofReal of that finite nonnegative density. Converting to real therefore gives exactly the actual density a.e.; null-set choices cannot change the affinity integral.
steps.lean: hPRN/hNRN use Measure.rnDeriv_withDensity on hPD/hND. hFG uses those a.e. identities and ENNReal.toReal_ofReal; the absolute-continuity outputs use withDensity_absolutelyContinuous.

steps.title: Establish genuine L1 before transporting the integral
steps.text: The normalized-density comparison theorem yields integrability of the square-root product of the actual split densities. Pull it back through the actual volume-preserving split and apply the a.e. RN identity. The change of variables follows from the measurable pushforward identity.
steps.formula: G=\sqrt{Q_+Q_-}\in L^1,\qquad F\in L^1(dx),\qquad\int F\,dx=\int G\,d(x_1,\ldots,x_k,z).
steps.lean: hGi calls the one shared DensityAffinity.normalized_density_tv_affinity with all hypotheses discharged from Ex70; hvol.integrable_comp_of_integrable and hFG give ambient L1. htrans applies integral_map_of_stronglyMeasurable and the actual hvol.map_eq.

steps.title: Separate the common residual and the block factors
steps.text: Nonnegativity of the actual block densities allows square roots to distribute over their finite product. The residual density is common to both signs and nonnegative, so the square root of its square is itself. This algebra also holds in the zero-dimensional unit-factor case.
steps.lean: MixtureDensities.actual_mixture_densities supplies hqpos0/hqneg0. hφ0 is direct positivity of the literal residual formula. hfactor uses Finset.prod_mul_distrib, Real.sqrt_mul, Real.sqrt_sq and Real.sqrt_prod.

steps.title: Integrate the independent factors
steps.text: Finite-product Fubini gives unit mass for the positive block-density product. Together with the already proved unit mass of the actual Ex70 split density, binary Fubini yields integral one for the common residual factor, including dimension zero. Applying the same product rules to the affinity factors leaves one copy of the block integral per block. The focused consumer combines this equality with the previously proved Eq25 estimate to bound the actual ambient-law affinity.
steps.lean: hblocks1 and hφ1 use integral_fintype_prod_volume_eq_pow, actual block unit mass, actual hP1 and integral_prod_mul with the canonical product-volume equality. The final calc uses hFG/htrans/hfactor and the same finite-product integral theorem. Tests.GaussianComplexityAffinityTensorization is a true-law RN-integral decay consumer; Eq25 is not an ancestor of the tensorization proof.
